stage: Stage 4 transfer gate (hard go/no-go before the generator)
benchmark: zero-shot transfer of the McGeary-trained off-target predictor to the real siRNA off-target studies (GSE184929 / GSE164289 / GSE196839), versus the mechanistic SeedMatchR / seed-match-count baseline on the same data

pre_registered.criterion_1: learned mean per-condition Spearman beats the mechanistic seed-count baseline by at least margin_spearman
pre_registered.criterion_2: reproduces the (S)-GNA KS direction on GSE184929: the model predicts MORE off-target for the parent D1 than for the (S)-GNA-destabilized D4, matching the measured shift
pre_registered.decision_rule: PASS only if BOTH criteria hold; otherwise FAIL and do not build the generator

criterion_2_sgna_direction.note: the predictor uses the same seed (count + seed-duplex dG) for D1 and D4, so its features are identical for the parent and the (S)-GNA guide; it cannot distinguish the (S)-GNA destabilization and predicts the same off-target for both

decision: FAIL: the McGeary-trained predictor does NOT beat the mechanistic seed-count baseline (delta below the pre-registered margin) and cannot reproduce the (S)-GNA direction. Per the staged playbook, do NOT build the generator on this predictor; publish the predictor plus the honest negative transfer result and stop before Stage 5.
supports: Stage 4 hard gate; the empirically measured miRNA->siRNA domain-adaptation (Ben-David) transfer term of the composition theorem, reported not assumed
